facts.fact: Sajan (Second Guard) and Sanu (Fourth Guard) are brothers from Pallikara, sold two years apart to different houses; Sajan's intake roll names a younger brother sold at seven. Neither knew until Neela read the rolls. Sanu wants to self-name to Sajan; Sajan says he would bleed for him and would rather not.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Sanu wanting to name himself to his brother.

facts.fact: Lata (Third Guard) refused her page in ch 16 but rode north anyway, joining at the Salt Gate at dusk, so the riders number twenty-two with her (one of the twenty-two who agreed stayed behind).
facts.why: needed because the beat has Lata argue for the offer while the riders number twenty-two.

facts.fact: Neela took Chathu's tin of sweets from his cell and ate one there; she has not eaten another.
facts.why: needed because the beat has the tin in her saddlebag and says she has eaten no further sweet.

facts.fact: The ride from Kodiyur to the shoulder above the pass takes four days; the Company's 'nobody smears' order holds on the road, so no one turns.
facts.why: needed to place arrival at dusk and keep witness rules intact.

facts.fact: Neela reinterprets the jackal call 'tomorrow, I will find you' as 'wait, I will be found', not a goodbye.
